newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen continuing volatile this week.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen continuing volatile this week.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to remain volatile this week, torn between blue-chip buying and the sell-off of shares in sectors which may be struggling with financial concerns such as banks and construction, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average lost 2.6 percent of its worth last week, finishing on Friday at 17,867.04. Japanese markets will reopen on Wednesday.

"Distrust in the construction and bank sectors were renewed as rumours of financial woes at Nippon Credit Bank and Tobishima Corp dragged the market under with them," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
Brokers said jitters over the health of the banking and construction sectors would weigh on stocks again this week.
Brokers were also concerned that selective buying of blue-chips, which has tempered some of the market's recent hemorrhaging, could dry up.
"If profit-taking of the high-flying blue chips sets in on top of the weakness in domestic sector shares, the losses could be pretty hefty," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
"But the possibility of a plunge to the 14,000 level is unlikely," she added.
Market sources see a floor on the market at 17,300, a recent closing low. Any gains are expected to be capped at 18,300.

Anxiety over the feeble state of the shares in sectors saddled with bad loans was so acute that even the sharply weaker yen has taken a back seat, brokers said. "Investors believe a weaker yen will boost the performance of export-related firms, especially bellwether issues," Kondo said. "But attention seems to be more on Japan's financial sector worries than on currencies at the moment."
However, some analysts said the focus could shift back to the dollar, which rose to a fresh 48-month high of 124.30 yen in Tokyo on Friday.

"Eyes will be on spectacular moves by currencies and U.S. stock market as well, since a sharp slide (in the yen or the Dow) could do serious psychological damage to the already-fragile Tokyo stock market," said Akihiro Naemura, strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
The Dow gained 82.74 points on Friday to close at 6,855.80 buoyed by steady U.S. jobs data combined with last week's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged.
